beats.text: Birds sit on power lines all day and never get zapped. Why?
Electricity only flows when there's a voltage difference. Like water, it needs a slope.
A bird on one wire touches just one voltage. Both feet are at the same level.
So the current stays in the wire. The wire is the easy path.
But touch two wires, or a wire and the pole, and it's a different story.
That's why big birds are most at risk, and why crews fit covers.
It's not about the bird. It's about the difference.
